title: Cirrus Health - Proof-of-Concept Quality Sprint Plan
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark matrix and sample golden prompts by 2027-10-08
Cirrus to share 150 representative queries and 10 red team prompts by 2027-10-11
Set up benchmark run (initial load tests) week of 2027-10-18
Schedule follow-up to review initial results on 2027-10-25
action_items: Maya Chen: Email benchmark template + SLO checklist (due 2027-10-08)
Liam Ortiz: Draft latency/cost model and baseline queries for load plan (due 2027-10-12)
Priya Patel: Provide data sensitivity notes and list of must-pass clinical formats (due 2027-10-11)
Ethan Ross: Provision staging VPC and test endpoints (due 2027-10-15)
summary: Kickoff for POC quality and performance sprint. Focused on defining golden-casebook, regression playlist, hallucination/format checks, scoring rubric, success criteria and a two-week benchmark cadence. Raised data residency and SOC2 concerns; aligned on on-prem vs hosted fallback. Agreed next steps and owners.
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Okay thanks everyone for joining. I think we can get started. We have about an hour, want to nail down acceptance criteria and the sprint plan for the PoC quality work.
[00:18] Priya Patel: Hi all, thanks. Quick note, our timelines a bit compressed — leadership wants a go/no-go after two weeks of bench results. So success criteria need to be concrete.

[00:32] Liam Ortiz: Understood. We'll propose a two-week cadence: week one golden-set + regression baseline, week two load + final pass. We also want to capture hallucination metrics and format conformance for clinical outputs.

[00:47] Ethan Ross: For context our platform handles discharge summaries and triage notes. So format checks are strict — templates must match, ICD codes in structured fields etc. We care not just about hallucination but also deterministic slot filling.
[01:05] Dr. Sunita Rao: And clinically, hallucinations that invent medications or contraindications are blockers. Our acceptance bar is high there.

[01:20] Maya Chen: Great. I'll read out a proposed success rubric, and then Liam will walk through sample benchmarks. High level: functional correctness (golden pass rate >= 92%), hallucination gates (zero critical clinical hallucinations in golden set), latency and cost SLOs (p95 < 450ms for 90% of queries at baseline traffic), and regression stability (no >3% drop vs baseline on core metrics).
[01:49] Priya Patel: 92% feels tight but ok if we define the golden-casebook well. Who owns labeling for the golden set?

[02:01] Maya Chen: We'll propose an initial golden deck from Redwood — about 200 golden prompts representative of your top cases — you can refine. Ownership: Redwood drafts, Cirrus reviews and finalizes.
[02:18] Priya Patel: That works. We'll need to include corner cases — pediatrics, renal dosing — flagged as must-pass items.

[02:33] Liam Ortiz: On the technical side, benchmark matrix: we'll run three classes of tests — functional (golden set), regression (random sample of 2k queries), and load (concurrent steady-state + spikes). For load targets you mentioned earlier, Ethan, what peak QPS should we target?
[02:51] Ethan Ross: Our prod peak is roughly 40 QPS for inference across triage, but for the PoC we want to test 2x headroom so aim for 80 QPS sustained and a 200 QPS spike for 2 minutes.
[03:05] Liam Ortiz: Got it. We'll configure the load harness accordingly. Expected token-length distribution? That affects KV cache behavior and throughput.
[03:15] Priya Patel: Average payloads ~180 tokens, tail up to 1,200 tokens for full notes. Important: long context correctness matters for follow-ups.
[03:28] Maya Chen: Note, runtime choices: you can run on Redwood Hosted for speed, or Dedicated / Private for data residency. Priya, you mentioned SOC2 and on-prem constraints?

[03:40] Priya Patel: Yes — for the PoC it's okay to start on Redwood hosted staging if data is anonymized. For production we'd need VPC/private deployment and KMS-managed keys. We need to see audit log capabilities.
[03:58] Maya Chen: We'll attach our SOC2 and audit log docs. For the PoC we can support a VPC stub or ephemeral staging VPC to run realistic runs.
[04:10] Ethan Ross: Good. One technical ask: can we pin model variants? We may want a quantized variant for cost testing and a full float for quality comparison.
[04:21] Liam Ortiz: Yes, our runtime supports model variants and fallbacks. We'll include both in the benchmark plan; cost/latency delta will be reported token-level.
[04:34] Priya Patel: How will hallucination be measured? Manual review? automated heuristics?

[04:41] Liam Ortiz: Combination. Golden set will be human-labeled with graded severity: critical (e.g., wrong meds), major (incorrect fact that impacts decisions), minor (stylistic). We'll compute a severity-weighted hallucination score. Additionally, we'll run automated checks for out-of-schema outputs and missing required fields.
[04:59] Dr. Sunita Rao: For clinical outputs, even a single critical hallucination on the golden set is a blocker. We can't accept that.
[05:08] Maya Chen: Noted — we'll set a hard gate: zero critical hallucinations on golden-casebook. For major hallucinations we expect <2% in golden set.
[05:19] Priya Patel: For regression testing, how frequent are runs and what does "regression stability" mean numerically?

[05:27] Liam Ortiz: We'll run daily automated regression on anonymized replay traffic during the sprint. Stability threshold: no more than a 3% drop in semantic-similarity metrics on core intents, and response-format pass rate >= 98%.
[05:43] Ethan Ross: What similarity metric are you using? BLEU? Embedding cosine?
[05:48] Liam Ortiz: Embedding-based similarity (cosine) plus a heuristics matcher for required slots. We'll report both. The rubric will show per-intent thresholds.
[05:57] Priya Patel: On scoring: can we get a single composite score to show leadership? Helpful to summarize tradeoffs (quality vs cost).

[06:05] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll publish a composite PoC score: weighted sum of Quality (50%), Safety/hallucination (30%), and Ops (latency/cost) (20%). We'll provide the weights and allow you to adjust them before the run.
[06:21] Priya Patel: Sounds fair. Timeline recap?

[06:24] Maya Chen: Week 0 (this week): finalize golden prompts and provide data notes. Week 1: golden + regression baseline runs, manual review of golden outputs. Week 2: load tests and variant cost comparisons, final report and decision. Deliverable at end: benchmark report, golden-casebook with annotations, regression playlist, and suggested production config.
[06:43] Ethan Ross: For instrumentation, we'll need per-route token counts and per-token cost breakdowns. Also request trace IDs in logs to correlate failed cases.
[06:55] Liam Ortiz: We'll enable detailed tracing for the PoC and include a token-level cost table in the report.
[07:02] Priya Patel: Any legal/procurement blockers for spinning up a short staging account?
[07:07] Maya Chen: For the two-week PoC, standard NDA covers shared artifacts. We can use ephemeral credentials and rotate keys. We'll also provide a data processing addendum if needed.
[07:19] Dr. Sunita Rao: One more clinical ask: can the scoring show example failures for each severity so we can triage quickly?
[07:26] Liam Ortiz: Yes, the golden review will include a failure catalogue with diffed outputs and suggested prompt tweaks.
[07:34] Priya Patel: About golden prompts — do you accept red-team prompts that intentionally induce hallucination? We want to ensure worst-case coverage.
[07:41] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We encourage a red-team subset — those will be labeled separately and used for safety gates.
[07:48] Ethan Ross: Ok logistics: we'll assemble the 150 queries and 10 red-team prompts by monday. Can your team provide a template for anonymization and a sample CSV schema?
[07:58] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll send the CSV template and an example pipeline for de-identification.
[08:05] Priya Patel: One last item: are there any known model behaviors with long context we should expect?

[08:11] Liam Ortiz: Longer contexts may see token recency bias and slight degradation in entity recall; we'll call out these failure modes and recommend prompt engineering and KV-cache tuning. Also note that quantized variants may slightly increase hallucination risk on edge cases — we'll quantify that.

[08:29] Maya Chen: Alright, recap of action items — I'll email the benchmark plan and golden prompt starter pack by Friday (2027-10-08). Priya and team to deliver query corpus by Monday (2027-10-11). Liam to set up load harness and instrument tracing. Ethan to provision staging network. We'll reconvene 2027-10-25 to review results. Anything else?
[08:50] Priya Patel: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[08:54] Maya Chen: Thanks, talk soon.
